questions.q: What three conditions make a conversation "crucial"?
a: High stakes, differing opinions and strong emotions
Low stakes, shared opinions and calm emotions
High stakes, shared opinions and strong emotions
Low stakes, differing opinions and calm emotions
questions.why: The overview defines a crucial conversation as one where stakes are high, opinions vary and emotions run strong.

questions.q: What two unhelpful ways do people react when they stop feeling safe?
a: Silence or violence
Silence or agreement
Violence or compromise
Agreement or avoidance
questions.why: Lesson 1 says that when safety disappears, people move toward either silence or violence.

questions.q: Why does the summary advise remembering your goal during a tense discussion?
a: It keeps you from reacting emotionally and losing sight of a solution
It gives you a way to win the argument quickly
It shows the other person that you are not listening
It lets you avoid the conversation entirely
questions.why: Lesson 1 says focusing on your purpose and the information you want to convey keeps anger in check.

questions.q: What does the AMPP acronym suggest you do to listen well?
a: Ask, mirror, paraphrase and prime
Ask, memorize, persuade and propose
Agree, mirror, promise and perform
Argue, manage, placate and proceed
questions.why: Lesson 2 lays out the four listening steps as ask, mirror, paraphrase and prime.

questions.q: What is the first step of the STATE method?
a: Share the facts rather than your interpretation of them
Tell your story before anyone shares any facts
Ask the other person to agree with your view
Encourage the other person to stay silent
questions.why: Lesson 3 starts STATE with sharing facts, then telling your story, asking for theirs and talking tentatively.
